articles.title: Moderna shares plunge after cancer vaccine data leaks — despite positive results
articles.summary: Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck. Shares of both drugmakers fell even though the data, released in full later Thursday following the leak, appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations.

articles.title: OpenAI nears up to $30 billion funding round at $1.25 trillion valuation led by UAE investors
articles.summary: OpenAI is closing in on a funding round that could value the artificial intelligence giant at more than $1 trillion ahead of a potential initial public offering. The San Francisco-based AI company is raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, according to people familiar with the deal, who asked not to be named because the details were confidential.

articles.title: A lesson from poker tells us not to fold on Meta after its earnings sell-off. Here’s why
articles.summary: Meta's strong quarterly results were overshadowed by artificial intelligence spending concerns on Thursday, sending shares down 7%. The newest reason arrived alongside Wednesday's earnings release: Meta plans to create new Class C non-voting shares that the company can use to fund its AI infrastructure plans.

articles.title: AI debt and French bonds face a stress test — why it may not be over
articles.summary: From AI companies financing data center projects to France's heavily indebted government, credit markets are flashing warnings as investors grow warier of borrowing risks. Pressure is building in bond markets as investors demand more compensation to finance public debt. Softbank is a major AI investor with a large stake in OpenAI and investments in data centers and power infrastructure, including an $87 billion commitment for data centers in France.

articles.title: Bill Ackman says 2027 will be an amazing year for stocks as wars, inflation ease
articles.summary: Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman said two geopolitical conflicts — the Ukraine-Russia and Iran wars — along with elevated inflation and interest rates are holding back an otherwise "booming market environment." "Once the overhang of the war is done — and it sounds like we're also potentially heading in the right direction with Russia-Ukraine — energy prices could come way down, and obviously that would be very good for inflation and markets," Ackman told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on...

articles.title: We're dipping back into the AI trade with our first data center buy in weeks
articles.summary: Following the trade, Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust will own 100 shares of GEV, increasing its weighting in the portfolio to about 2.15% from 1.9%. AI-related semiconductors and industrial stocks are getting hit hard as investors grow increasingly concerned about the source of capital to support the data center buildout.
